children: Citi's clients in Japan and South Korea feel it is unfair for MSCI to reclassify Indonesia as a frontier or standalone market, given its governance reforms, says analyst Ferry Wong in a note. The bank puts the chances of Indonesia staying in MSCI's emerging-markets index at roughly 50:50. Exclusion could trigger $4 billion to $5 billion of passive outflows and $8 billion to $10 billion from active funds. Citi's top picks include conglomerate Astra International for its strong payouts and Bank Central Asia due to its strong deposit franchise. The Jakarta Composite Index closed at 5146.33 on Friday, and is down 40.5% year to date. (venkat.pr@wsj.com)
